text.en: Asha counted dozens of bananas and said, "Chemists count atoms in moles, just like we count in dozens."

Atoms are very small, so we compare their masses with the carbon-12 atom. Relative atomic mass is the ratio of the average mass of an atom of an element to one-twelfth of the mass of a carbon-12 atom, and the average atomic mass is the weighted average over natural isotopes. A molecule is the smallest particle of a substance that can exist freely, and the relative molecular mass is the sum of the atomic masses.
One mole of any substance contains 6.023 x 10^23 particles, which is Avogadro's number, and its mass in grams is the gram atomic mass or gram molecular mass. The number of moles = mass / molar mass. Percent composition tells the percentage by mass of each element in a compound.
Avogadro's hypothesis states that equal volumes of all gases under the same conditions of temperature and pressure contain the same number of molecules. Vapour density is related to relative molecular mass by molecular mass = 2 x vapour density.

problem.en: How many moles are in 36 g of water (molar mass 18 g)?

prompt.en: A friend says One mole of oxygen and one mole of hydrogen contain different numbers of molecules. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: One mole of any substance has 6.023 x 10^23 particles.
So the number is the same.

points.en: Equal volumes of gases have equal molecules.
